items.claim: Ezek.26.15-26.21 holds one literary movement, and merging the princes' dismay with the deep-waters verdict is what the bytes support. The messenger speech at MT 26:19 addresses the same feminine-singular referent as MT 26:15-18 (“הֲלֹ֣א מִקּ֣וֹל מַפַּלְתֵּ֗ךְ” at 26:15 against “בְּתִתִּ֤י אֹתָךְ֙ עִ֣יר נֶחֱרֶ֔בֶת” at 26:19), so no addressee changes there; MT 26:18 ends “עַתָּה֙ יֶחְרְד֣וּ הָֽאִיִּ֔ן י֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּ֑ךְ” and carries no member of the recognition, utterance or emphatic-spoken families, so nothing refrain-grade stands behind the messenger formula that follows — both of the conditions that would license a cut at a messenger formula fail. The span's only formula-grade close is the utterance signature “נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה” at MT 26:21. The lament noun at MT 26:17 is reported third-person speech of the sea-princes (“וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרוּ לָ֔ךְ”), not a command to the prophet, which is the discriminator the book itself uses at MT 27:2 and MT 28:12 where the prophet is told to raise one; reading it as texture rather than a genre onset is right. The held medium_low is earned by the setumah after MT 26:18, the one real tension inside the span, and is not overstated.
items.both_sides: Close side behind the onset: MT 26:14 stacks the full emphatic clause “כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי” with the utterance signature and the setumah follows that verse — the strongest close in the chapter, so the onset at MT 26:15 is earned from the far side. Onset side of the rival interior cut at MT 26:19: a messenger formula with no change of addressee, behind a verse with no closing formula, leaving the setumah after MT 26:18 as the only signal — and Masoretic paragraphing informs without deciding. Close side of the row: the utterance signature at MT 26:21 with a setumah after it, and a fresh word-event onset at MT 27:1 ahead. The chapter's whole poetic texture (eight lineated lines, every one of them inside 26:17-18) is translation-layer and is correctly kept out of the seam question.

suggested_fix.fact: no change; the lament noun inside the span is reported speech of the sea-princes and is texture, not a genre onset, and the span's only formula-grade close stands at its last verse

items.claim: The warrant for holding all 36 verses as one row states that no formula marks any internal point in the chapter, and a messenger formula stands inside the span at MT 27:3 (“כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה”, after “וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לְצ֗וֹר”), so a verse inside this row belongs to the 122-verse messenger census. The absence claim carries no count and is false as written. The keep is nonetheless right, for a reason the row does not give: a messenger formula licenses a cut only where the addressee changes or a refrain close stands immediately before it, and at MT 27:3 the addressee is the same Tyre named in the lament command at MT 27:2, with no close behind it. Second fact in the same row: the rival interior cuts are dismissed as plain lineated continuations at both candidate points, and the translation changes texture at both — lineation ends at web:Ezek.27.11 and web:Ezek.27.12 begins prose behind a paragraph break, and the prose list ends at web:Ezek.27.24 with lineation resuming at web:Ezek.27.25. That layer should carry no weight in a rival rejection at all, and here the mis-stated version of it is what makes the rejection read clean.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the word-event onset in its contiguous form at MT 27:1 with the prophet's lament command “שָׂ֥א עַל צֹ֖ר קִינָֽה” at MT 27:2; behind it the utterance signature and setumah at MT 26:21 close the preceding chapter. Close side: MT 27:36 carries no member of the closing formula families and rests on the setumah after it plus its own terminal clause “בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד עוֹלָֽם”, with a fresh word-event onset at MT 28:1 ahead. What actually defeats the two candidate interior seams is that neither point carries an onset device and neither carries a Masoretic mark — the chapter's single mark follows its last verse — and that a lament-labelled unit is not split.

The verse reads “כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי”, without the divine name, and that shorter clause stands on 4 verses of the book (MT 23:34, 26:5, 28:10, 39:5), while the full form “כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי”, quoted here from MT 26:14, is what the 14 are built on. The row's machine-readable signal for the emphatic close rests on the same misassignment. The seam is unaffected: MT 28:10 still carries the utterance signature and the setumah follows it, so the close holds on one closing formula rather than two stacked ones.

items.claim: The close-side corroboration says the terminal clause at MT 28:19 mirrors MT 27:36 exactly, and names no tier. The two are identical at the consonantal skeleton and differ in the pointing, which is where the gender sits: MT 27:36 reads “בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד עוֹלָֽם” of a feminine addressee and MT 28:19 reads “בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם” of a masculine one. The recurrence is real and it is this row's best close evidence, because MT 28:19 carries no member of the closing formula families at all; what it needs is its tier named. The nearest relative of the clause, MT 26:21 (“בַּלָּה֥וֹת אֶתְּנֵ֖ךְ וְאֵינֵ֑ךְ”, a different verb), is not part of the pair and should not be folded into it.

Close side: MT 28:19 with a petuchah after it, named as a petuchah and correctly not merged with the setumah class, and a fresh word-event onset at MT 28:20 ahead. The finding changes neither side; it changes the tier at which the close-side recurrence is claimed.

items.claim: The row places the addressee shift in two incompatible places. Its close-side reading and its rival rejection both put the turn to the house of Israel inside MT 28:24 — correctly, since that verse opens “וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל” and holds no address to Sidon at all, its pronouns being third-person plural of Israel's neighbours — while the disclosure field says the recognition clauses at MT 28:22 and 28:23 are paragraph-final rather than row-final because MT 28:24 continues the same verdict before the addressee shifts. Both cannot be true, and the seam turns on exactly that fact. Second: the rival cut at MT 28:23/28:24 is rejected with the setumah as the operative discriminator, where a tier-1 ground settles it — MT 28:24 carries no onset device of any class the book uses to open a unit (no dateline, no word-event in any of its three forms, no hand-of-YHWH, no transport verb, no messenger formula, no set-your-face, no son-of-man address, no behold-I-am-against clause), so no row can open there, while MT 28:25 carries the messenger formula with the addressee changed. Span and confidence both stand.
items.both_sides: Close side: MT 28:24 ends on the Adonai-form recognition clause “וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה”, a variant standing on 5 verses of the book (MT 13:9, 23:49, 24:24, 28:24, 29:16) — the row's count of five verifies — with the setumah after that verse and none after MT 28:23. Onset side of the rival: MT 28:24 has no onset device, so the rival would have a row open on a verse the book gives no way of opening; the strict recognition clause at MT 28:23 (“וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה”) is a close, and a close alone does not manufacture the onset the next row would need. Ahead: the messenger formula at MT 28:25, standing behind the refrain close of MT 28:24, satisfies both conditions for a cut at a messenger formula.

suggested_fix.fact: the turn to the house of Israel falls inside the row's last verse, which names the house of Israel and holds no address to Sidon, and the row closes on the Adonai-form recognition clause standing there

items.claim: The under-three-verse warrant rests on the MT 33:21-22 case and describes that case as a messenger onset with a recognition close and a setumah. None of the three holds there: MT 33:21 is one of the book's 14 year-bearing datelines (“בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ”) carrying the fugitive's report, MT 33:22 is the hand-of-YHWH mouth-opening (“וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י”), neither verse carries a recognition clause, and the Masoretic mark after MT 33:22 is a petuchah, not a setumah — two classes this corpus never merges. That case is also one the book's own plan leaves open, so it cannot carry another row's warrant. The span itself is right on its own evidence and should rest there: MT 28:25 carries the messenger formula (“כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒”) with the addressee changed to the house of Israel, the refrain close stands in MT 28:24 immediately behind it — the two conditions that license a cut at a messenger formula — and MT 28:26 closes on the fullest recognition clause in the book's repertoire (“וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם”) with a setumah after it.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the messenger formula at MT 28:25 with a changed addressee, standing behind the Adonai-form recognition close of MT 28:24 and the setumah after that verse. Close side: the recognition clause naming YHWH as their God at MT 28:26 with a setumah after it, and a year-bearing dateline opening the next unit at MT 29:1, a hard seam on any reading. Both sides of this row are formula-bearing, which is what makes the two-verse length defensible; what does not survive is the borrowed warrant, since the case it borrows from has neither of the two devices attributed to it and carries the other mark class.

suggested_fix.fact: the two-verse span is warranted by its own onset, a messenger formula with the addressee changed to the house of Israel standing behind the refrain close of the preceding verse, and not by the dateline-and-hand case at MT 33:21-22, whose mark is a petuchah
